newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland urged not to foresake inflation for growth.
newsitem.headline: Poland urged not to foresake inflation for growth.

text.p: European Monetary Institute (EMI) president Alexandre Lamfalussy warned Poland on Tuesday that its impressive economic growth may be jeopardised unless inflation is significantly lowered.

"You are now in a good situation in a sense of strong economic growth but be careful, this may not last if you do not manage to curb inflation," Lamfalussy told reporters after meeting Polish central bank president Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz.

The Polish government, though trying to cut inflation to 17 percent in December this year from 21.6 percent last year, gives priority to maintaining economic growth, which reached seven percent in 1995, over a radical reduction in inflation.
Gronkiewicz-Waltz confirmed the central bank's view that no radical inflation cut would be possible without a complete elimination of the budget deficit coupled with a slow-down of economic growth.
"The budget deficit is in our situation the main factor creating money supply, which makes it difficult to substantially cut inflation," she told reporters.
Poland targets this year's budget deficit to amount to 2.6 percent of gross domestic product, slightly lower than in 1995.

Gronkiewicz-Waltz noted that a budget deficit below three percent of GDP was one of the criteria Poland fulfilled of the future European Monetary Union (EMU). Another one was its public debt amounting to less 60 percent of GDP.
Lamfalussy, ending his visit to Poland, earlier briefed Gronkiewicz-Waltz on planned mechanisms of introducing EMU.

He said Poland would be welcome to apply to join the EMU, scheduled to take effect in 1999 in those European Union countries with the most stable currencies, after it becomes a EU member. The European Commission says this is unlikely to happen before 2002.

Lamfalussy, whose EMI is a forerunner to the Eurpean Central Bank, confirmed that latest views on a European Rate Mechansim would be unveiled a meeting of EU finance ministers and central bank governors in Dublin on September 20 and 21.
